topics.title: Law of large numbers and the CLT

concepts.name: Ordinary least squares
concepts.summary: OLS picks the line that minimizes the sum of squared residuals.

concepts.name: Slope = Cov(X,Y) / Var(X)
concepts.summary: In simple regression the OLS slope equals the sample covariance of X and Y divided by the variance of X.

concepts.name: Residuals
concepts.summary: A residual is the gap between an observed value and the fitted value from the regression line.

concepts.name: Gauss–Markov assumptions
concepts.summary: Linearity, random sampling, no perfect collinearity, zero conditional mean, and constant error variance.

concepts.name: Homoskedasticity
concepts.summary: The error term has the same variance for every value of the regressors: Var(u|X) = σ².

concepts.name: BLUE
concepts.summary: Under Gauss–Markov, OLS is the best linear unbiased estimator: lowest variance among linear unbiased estimators.

concepts.name: Omitted variable bias
concepts.summary: Leaving out a variable that is correlated with X and affects Y biases the OLS slope.

concepts.name: Partial effect
concepts.summary: A coefficient in multiple regression measures the effect of one regressor holding the others fixed.

concepts.name: t-statistic
concepts.summary: t = (estimate − hypothesized value) / standard error, compared with a t distribution.

concepts.name: F-test
concepts.summary: The F-test checks whether several coefficients are jointly zero by comparing restricted and unrestricted fits.

concepts.name: p-value
concepts.summary: The probability, under the null hypothesis, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the one observed.

concepts.name: Dummy variable trap
concepts.summary: Including a dummy for every category plus an intercept creates perfect collinearity.

concepts.name: Interaction term
concepts.summary: A product of two regressors lets the effect of one depend on the level of the other.

concepts.name: Autocorrelation
concepts.summary: Errors in different time periods are correlated, so usual OLS standard errors are wrong.

concepts.name: Durbin–Watson test
concepts.summary: A test for first-order autocorrelation in regression residuals; values near 2 suggest none.

concepts.name: Random variable
concepts.summary: A function that assigns a number to each outcome of a random experiment.

concepts.name: Probability mass function
concepts.summary: For a discrete random variable, the PMF gives P(X = x) for each value x.

concepts.name: Expected value
concepts.summary: The probability-weighted average of a random variable: E[X] = Σ x·P(X = x).

concepts.name: Variance
concepts.summary: How far a random variable spreads around its mean: Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − (E[X])².

concepts.name: Linearity of expectation
concepts.summary: E[aX + bY] = aE[X] + bE[Y], whether or not X and Y are independent.

concepts.name: Normal distribution
concepts.summary: The bell-shaped distribution fully described by its mean μ and variance σ².

concepts.name: Binomial distribution
concepts.summary: The number of successes in n independent trials with success probability p.

concepts.name: Covariance
concepts.summary: Cov(X,Y) = E[(X − μX)(Y − μY)] measures how two variables move together.

concepts.name: Correlation coefficient
concepts.summary: Covariance rescaled to lie between −1 and 1.

concepts.name: Law of large numbers
concepts.summary: The sample mean converges to the population mean as the sample grows.

concepts.name: Central limit theorem
concepts.summary: The standardized sample mean is approximately normal for large n, whatever the population shape.

concepts.name: Standard error
concepts.summary: The standard deviation of an estimator’s sampling distribution.

concepts.name: Confidence interval
concepts.summary: A range built so that it covers the true parameter in a stated share of repeated samples.

concepts.name: Integration by parts
concepts.summary: ∫u dv = uv − ∫v du, useful for products such as x·e^x.

concepts.name: Improper integral
concepts.summary: An integral over an infinite interval or with an unbounded integrand, defined as a limit.

concepts.name: Comparison test
concepts.summary: An improper integral converges if it is bounded by one that converges.

concepts.name: Geometric series
concepts.summary: Σ arⁿ converges to a/(1 − r) when |r| < 1.

concepts.name: Ratio test
concepts.summary: A series converges absolutely if the limit of |a(n+1)/a(n)| is below 1.

concepts.name: Taylor polynomial
concepts.summary: A polynomial that matches a function and its first n derivatives at a point.

concepts.name: Remainder term
concepts.summary: The error between a function and its Taylor polynomial, bounded by the next derivative.

chunks.text: The OLS estimates minimize the sum of squared residuals Σ(yᵢ − b₀ − b₁xᵢ)².
The slope estimate can be written as b₁ = Cov(x, y) / Var(x).
Set ∂/∂b₁ Σ(yᵢ − b₀ − b₁xᵢ)² = 0 → b₁ = Σ(xᵢ − x̄)(yᵢ − ȳ) / Σ(xᵢ − x̄)².
The slope tells us how much y changes on average when x goes up by one unit.
The residual is what is left over: the actual value minus the fitted value.
MLR.5 Homoskedasticity: Var(u | x₁, …, xₖ) = σ². The error variance does not depend on the regressors.
Under MLR.1–MLR.5, OLS is BLUE: the best linear unbiased estimator.
Unbiased needs MLR.1–4. BLUE also needs homoskedasticity (MLR.5) — without it OLS is still unbiased but not the most efficient.
The first assumption is that the population process is linear in parameters.
Bias(b̃₁) = β₂ · δ̃₁, where δ̃₁ is the slope from regressing x₂ on x₁.
β₁ measures the effect of x₁ on y holding x₂ fixed — the ceteris paribus interpretation.
Omitting a relevant variable that is correlated with x₁ makes b₁ biased.
The test statistic is the estimate divided by its standard error, and we compare it to a t distribution with n − 2 degrees of freedom.
Q4. Test H₀: β₂ = β₃ = 0 using the F statistic from the restricted and unrestricted R².
So the F test asks: if I force these coefficients to zero, how much worse does the fit get?
With an intercept, include g − 1 dummies for g groups. Including all g creates perfect collinearity.
An interaction term lets the effect of one variable on the outcome depend on the value of another variable.
With AR(1) errors, uₜ = ρuₜ₋₁ + eₜ, OLS remains unbiased but the usual standard errors are invalid.
Durbin–Watson d ≈ 2(1 − ρ̂). Values near 2 indicate no first-order autocorrelation.
Autocorrelation means that the error in this period is correlated with the error in the previous period.
A random variable is a function X: Ω → ℝ assigning a number to every outcome.
The PMF p(x) = P(X = x) satisfies p(x) ≥ 0 and Σ p(x) = 1.
X = sum of two dice. P(X = 7) = 6/36, the most likely value.
The expected value is a weighted average of the possible values, weighted by their probabilities.
The variance is the expected squared distance from the mean, and a shortcut is E of X squared minus the mean squared.
E[aX + b] = aE[X] + b, and more generally expectation is linear.
Var(X) = E[(X − μ)²] = E[X²] − μ². Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X).
Var(X) = E[X² − 2μX + μ²] = E[X²] − 2μ² + μ² = E[X²] − μ².
X ~ Bin(n, p) has E[X] = np and Var(X) = np(1 − p).
The normal density f(x) = (1/σ√(2π)) exp(−(x − μ)²/2σ²) integrates to 1 over the real line.
The simplest case of a normal distribution is the standard normal distribution, with mean 0 and variance 1.
Cov(X, Y) = E[XY] − E[X]E[Y]. Independent variables have zero covariance.
Var(X + Y) = Var(X) + Var(Y) + 2Cov(X, Y).
ρ = Cov(X, Y) / (σX σY) always lies in [−1, 1]; ρ = ±1 only for an exact linear relationship.
Even when the data come from a uniform distribution, the means of many samples are normally distributed.
LLN says the average settles down to mu. CLT says how it wiggles around mu — normally, with spread sigma over root n.
The standard error of the sample mean is σ/√n, estimated by s/√n.
A 95% confidence interval for μ is x̄ ± 1.96·s/√n for large n.
95% of intervals built this way would contain μ — not “μ is in this interval with probability 0.95”.
∫u dv = uv − ∫v du. Choose u by LIATE: logs, inverse trig, algebraic, trig, exponential.
For x times e to the x, let u be x and dv be e to the x dx.
∫₁^∞ 1/xᵖ dx converges if and only if p > 1.
If 0 ≤ f ≤ g and ∫g converges, then ∫f converges.
Σ_{n≥0} arⁿ = a/(1 − r) for |r| < 1, and diverges otherwise.
Ratio test: L = lim |a(n+1)/a(n)|. L < 1 converges absolutely, L > 1 diverges.
If L = 1 the ratio test is inconclusive and another test is needed.
Each new term lets the polynomial match one more derivative of the function at that point.
|Rₙ(x)| ≤ M|x − a|ⁿ⁺¹ / (n + 1)!, where |f⁽ⁿ⁺¹⁾| ≤ M between a and x.
lim b→∞ ∫₀ᵇ e^(−x) dx = 1
Чем больше выборка n, тем уже доверительный интервал: ширина пропорциональна 1/√n.

links.rationale: The OLS slope is the covariance of X and Y scaled by the variance of X.
The denominator of the OLS slope is the variance of X.
The t-statistic divides an estimate by its standard error.
Large-sample p-values come from the normal distribution.
The normal density integrates to 1 over an infinite interval — an improper integral.
Expected values of continuous variables such as the exponential are computed with integration by parts.
The CLT justifies using t and normal critical values for regression coefficients.
Homoskedasticity is the fifth Gauss–Markov assumption.
OLS is BLUE only when errors are homoskedastic.
Variance is defined as an expected value of squared deviations.
Variance is the covariance of a variable with itself.
A confidence interval is the estimate plus or minus a multiple of its standard error.
Both break the Gauss–Markov error assumptions, one across observations and one in variance.
Taylor expansions are used in the delta method built on the CLT.
